The Indian Navy commissioned INS-Monk role the third anti-submarine warfare shallow
water craft built by Kochi in Shipyard Limited, CSL, Kochi, at the naval dockyard in Mumbai
today.
The induction of the indigenous warship marks an important step towards strengthening the
Navy's ability to detect and counter submarine threats in coastal and shallow waters.
The commissioning ceremony was presided over by Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, flag
officer commanding in chief of the Western naval command. Addressing the gathering, Vice-Admiral
Vatsayan said by 2034, around 60 per cent of the Navy's platforms were expected to have
an average age of less than 10 years, a report.
The iron is mangrove-less equipped with modern weapons and sensors including the
Abhayal Mount Sonar, lightweight torpedoes and indigenous anti-submarine rocket launcher
and the Marij advanced torpedo decoy system. The ship can operate alongside maritime patrol
aircrafts, helicopters and other warships to detect and counter submarine threats, named
after Mangrul, a coastal town, and a prominent fishing hubber in Gujarat-Junagar district.
The ship carried forward the legacy of erstwhile INS Mangrul, a minesweeper that served the
Indian Navy until April 2004.
Prachna Akashwani, Mumbai.
Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Khanth has said the doors of the Supreme Court
are open to everyone, and any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected
body is welcome. He said every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and the court
will hear their concerns and grant whatever relief is due under the law. Addressing the 33rd
Foundation Day of the NHRC in New Delhi, Justice Surya Khan said, the constitution has made
expansive promises to every citizen, including of dignity, equality, liberty and justice.
Responding to the Interblocks' demand for a meeting, Justice Surya Khan said he had
received a letter yesterday, requesting an appointment, and had replied last night explaining
why he was unable to meet them.
The doors of the Supreme Court are open to everyone. Any person, whether an ordinary
citizen or a member of an elected body, has the right to approach us. Every citizen
of India has this right. We will hear the grievances and address their concerns in
accordance with the law and the legal framework. I received the letter yesterday and
replied to it last night, and I have cited the reasons for expressing my inability to meet.
I have maintained the confidentiality of the letter.
I have maintained confidentiality of the letter.
Congress leader and leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabharahul Gandhi has said that
India blocked leaders will file a petition in the Supreme Court today against Chief
Election Commissioner Ganesh Kumar.
Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Mr. Gandhi said he and Congress President
Malik Arjun Khargay had written a letter to the Chief Justice of India expressing concerns
over the fairness of elections. He said a protest against the alleged theft of votes has been
underway in Delhi for several days, and people are being stopped from reaching Delhi.
Delhi Traffic Police has issued an advisory for the day of a protest march called by
opposition parties in the afternoon. In its advisory, the traffic police said, traffic
movement is likely to be affected at various stretches across the national capital during
the day, the entry and exit gates at six Delhi metro stations will remain closed till 4pm in view
of the opposition's protest. The Traffic Police advised commuters to plan their journeys in advance
and allow additional travel time. It also asked the motorists to avoid non-essential travel
through affected areas. Meanwhile security arrangements were beefed up in the national
capital ahead of an opposition protest march. Security has been tightened at the city's borders,
railway stations, bus terminals, and other sensitive locations to prevent unauthorized
gatherings and maintain law and order. Delhi Police has designated three new venues for protests
and demonstrations – Ramleela Ground, Burradi Ground, and CBD Ground in East Delhi. In an
order, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar announced that Janthar Mantar has been denotified
As a designated protest site, the Union Home Ministry had constituted a committee to identify suitable alternative venues to ensure citizens' rights to organize protests and demonstrations.

The BJP Mahila Morcha staged a protest in New Delhi today demanding action against Congress MP from Inner Manipur Dr. Agomcha Bimol Akhoja over allegations of sexual harassment involving female students at Jawaharlal Nehru University.
The BJP claimed that JNU dismissed Akwajam from his teaching position following an inquiry
into complaints filed by 11 female students.
Talking to reporters, BJP MP Basri Swaraj criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and
other senior party leaders for their elist silence on the matter.
The Centre has urged all states and union territories to ensure the prominent display
of rates charged for services and facilities offered by clinical establishments.
The move aims to empower patients to make informed health care decisions, prevent billing-related
disputes and strengthen trust in health care services.
Union Health Secretary Puneer Salela Srivastava has written a letter to the chief secretaries
of all states and UTs in this regard.
Emphasizing the importance of transparency in health care pricing, Ms. Srivastava noted
that the conspicuous display of rates will help patients and their families to understand
and the likely cost of treatment, make informed healthcare decisions and plan their medical
expenditure.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said over the past few years the government has focused
on achieving self-reliance and modernisation across all sectors, from weaponry and technology
to clothing, equipment and training.
Speaking on the occasion of the signing of an MOU between the Indian Army and the
Food Corporation of India in New Delhi today, Mr Singh said India now manufactures
As a significant share of its defence requirements domestically, he said, when the government
provides good food, proper equipment, quality training and adequate facilities to soldiers,
it helps boost their morale.
The welfare of our soldiers is not a peripheral issue for us.
It is an integral component of national security.
When we provide our soldiers with a good food, quality equipment, proper training
and adequate facilities, it's strengthening their morale.
and I believe that a soldier with a high morale can face any challenge fearlessly.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service,
a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva
and a relentless commitment that continues.
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan,
the government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal
of Avikasit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication
is transforming lives. Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this
vision has been translated into action through the International Yoga Day initiative.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi proposed to observing International Yoga Day at the United
Nations General Assembly in 2014. Following the proposal, the United Nations declared
June 21st as International Yoga Day. Since 2015, the day has been observed across the world.
This has given yoga a global recognition and increased awareness about physical health,
mental peace and a balanced lifestyle.
When we do yoga, we feel physically fit, mentally calm and emotionally content.
But it is not just about doing exercise on a mat. Yoga is a way of life,
a holistic approach to health and well-being, a way to mindfulness in thoughts and actions,
a way to live in harmony with self, with others and with nature."
Ministry of Ayush, along with various institutions, organizes awareness programs, mass yoga sessions
and training activities to take yoga to people across the country.
Dev Bhumi Uttarakhand shares a deep connection with yoga and spirituality.
spirituality. Rishikesh is renowned across the world as a major center for yoga and meditation.
Its spiritual heritage along with Himalayas and Ganga attracts people from India and abroad.
To promote this rich legacy, the Uttarakhand government has implemented the Yoga Policy
2025 in line with the yoga policies of the central government. The objective is to
develop Uttarakhand into an international hub for yoga and wellness. The state government
has targeted of developing five new yoga centers by 2030. The message of International
International Yoga Day is that yoga is not merely a form of exercise but a way of achieving
a healthy and balanced life.
The global recognition brought by Prime Minister Narendra Modi's initiative along with Uttarakhand's
rich yoga heritage is playing an important role in spreading this message across the
world.
Sakshi Singh, Akashwani News, Theradun.

Vice President Sipitaradakrishnan today said that in the interconnected world, international
cooperation is not merely a diplomatic choice, but it is a strategic necessity for peace,
security and prosperity of the world.
Addressing the 66th National Defence College course in New Delhi, Mr. Radhakrishnan said,
the essence of global collaboration lies in recognizing and respecting shared interests
and converting them into collective action.
He added that global problems like climate change and terrorism demand collective response.
I am very happy to see that the current 66th NDC course has 122 participants with a wide
spectrum of professional experience and expertise.
I welcome our distinguished participants from friendly foreign countries.
This diverse composition provides a unique opportunity for cross-national learning.
That is the great importance of this course.

Union Minister for the Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupendra Yadav today emphasized
the vision of Vikasit Bharat at 2047, which must integrate economic development with
ecological security.
Addressing the participants of the mid-career training of the Indian Forest Service
new Delhi today. He acknowledged IFS officers' contribution to safeguarding India's forests,
wildlife and ecological heritage. He identified human-wildlife conflict, forest fires, climate change
and balancing development with conservation. Saudi Arabia's King Khaled International Airport
in Riyadh was targeted by another attack on Sunday, with the General Authority of Civil
aviation reporting that injuries and damage assessments were underway.
The latest incident comes just a day after the attack on the airport, one of the deadliest
on Saudi Arabia in almost a decade.
The Indian Embassy in Duyadh has informed that an Indian national who was among eleven
Indians injured in the attack has died.
External Affairs Minister S.J.
Shankar expressed grief over the death, offering condolences to the bereaved family.
Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthi group claimed it had carried out four missile and drone operations
against Saudi targets in response to what it described as Saudi aggression against Yemen.
In Pakistan, violence has escalated in Khaybar-Baghdunkhwa province following the federal government's
imposition of emergency rule and suspension of the provincial government, led by jailed
former Prime Minister Imran Khan's Pakistan-Tahrir Khan South PTI.
Police firing and shelling was reported in several areas.
Protests broke out against the federal intervention.
Yesterday, the PTI's planned march to Islamabad
was disrupted amid a security crackdown.
Police reportedly arrested 59 PTI workers in Swabhi
and six in Khayber district.
